$comment: Shape for packages/rules requirement templates. Phase 1 item 3 seeds the top 20 categories in this format. plain_english must link source_url and never claim certainty — 'appears to apply' language.

requirements.title: Children's Product Certificate (CPC)
requirements.plain_english: Products made for children 12 and under generally need a Children's Product Certificate backed by testing at a CPSC-accepted lab before import. This appears to apply to your product because you told us it's used by kids.
requirements.self_check_hint: Ask your supplier for the CPC and the lab report behind it.

requirements.title: Lead & phthalates limits
requirements.plain_english: Children's products must meet federal lead content and phthalates limits. Test reports should show results per accessible component.
requirements.self_check_hint: Check your lab report covers total lead and the 8 restricted phthalates.

requirements.title: Tracking label on product & packaging
requirements.plain_english: Children's products need a permanent tracking label (manufacturer, date/batch, source) on the product and packaging.
requirements.self_check_hint: Look at a production sample photo — is the label molded/printed on?

requirements.title: FCC equipment authorization (SDoC or certification)
requirements.plain_english: Electronics that emit radio frequency — anything with WiFi/Bluetooth, and most powered devices — generally need FCC authorization before import and sale. Devices with intentional radios usually need certification with an FCC ID.
requirements.self_check_hint: If it has WiFi/Bluetooth, search the FCC ID printed on it in the FCC database.

requirements.title: Lithium battery shipping rules
requirements.plain_english: Products with lithium batteries face packaging, labeling, and documentation rules in transport (UN38.3 test summary).
requirements.self_check_hint: Ask your freight forwarder for the UN38.3 test summary from the battery maker.
